ideas.title: Why the Humpback Whale Hunts With a Bubble Net #Shorts
ideas.concept: Show how humpback whales blow a rising wall of bubbles to trap a school of fish before surging upward through the center.
ideas.hook: This whale does not chase fish—it traps them inside a net made of bubbles.
ideas.keyVisual: Real humpback whale bubble-net feeding footage: wide surface shot, tightening bubble spiral, then the whale lunging through the fish.

ideas.title: Why the Wombat Poops Perfect Cubes #Shorts
ideas.concept: Explain how different elasticity in the wombat intestine helps form cube-shaped droppings that do not roll away from its territory.
ideas.hook: This animal makes cube-shaped poop—and the reason is stranger than you think.
ideas.keyVisual: Real wombat walking and close-up habitat footage, with a brief clean macro or illustrated cutaway of the intestine and cube-shaped droppings.

ideas.title: Why the Chameleon Shoots Its Tongue Like a Spring #Shorts
ideas.concept: Reveal how elastic collagen tissue lets a chameleon launch its tongue faster than muscle alone could manage.
ideas.hook: A chameleon can fire its tongue faster than you can blink—and it does not rely on muscle power alone.
ideas.keyVisual: Real chameleon close-up locking onto prey, slow-motion tongue strike, and a simple side graphic showing the elastic tissue release.
